newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly may take writeoff for PCS - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly may take writeoff for PCS - WSJ.

text.p: Eli Lilly & Co may have to write off a large portion of its $4.1 billion acquisition of PCS Health Systems Inc, which has not been the boon to its bottom line that had been anticipated, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Thursday's electronic edition, the Journal said that in a recent government filing, Lilly said it is evaluating whether PCS, which it acquired in 1994, is worth "significantly less" than originally believed.
Company executives say privately that they will probably have to write off a portion of the investment as soon as the end of this month, the Journal said.
When PCS was acquired in 1994, Lilly Chief Executive Randall Tobias said it would stop diluting the parent company's earnings by late 1996.
Instead, PCS has not added to Lilly's earnings, and analysts say it is losing money after taking into account an estimated $275 million in yearly interest payouts.

The purchase "can only be called a monumental blunder," said Ken Langone, an investment banking executive and leading Lilly shareholder. "It's in everyone's interest that they call this a bad mistake and write this thing down."
The company said it still has faith that PCS will prove to have considerable value, but it will not comment while it re-evaluates PCS' worth.
